analysis.title: Marketcolour + UK Budget Pre / SAP / Maersk (dg) / Schindler / Galderma / SEB
key_insights: US equities closed higher Wednesday on a momentum chase: SPX +58bps to 7757, NDX +113bps to 29,822, RTY +27bps to 2781. Tech +1.61%, Industrials +0.91%, Comm Svcs -1.33%.
GS AI Software basket rose 3.98% and the GS Cyber Security basket rose 4.55%. Space names caught a bid, led by SPCX +7.8% on strong Q3 earnings.
EU Semis (GSSBSEMI) rose 2.7% after SpaceX and Super Micro prints overnight and a bullish Berlin keynote from Jensen Huang.

Mag7 lagged on competition concerns after SPCX results, rotation into SPCX, Cleveland checks weighing on GOOGL, and possible source-of-funds selling ahead of expected future issuance. Semis bounced but felt underwhelming after 10 of 11 sessions lower.

Hedge funds heavily net sold global equities so far in October, with short sales outpacing long buys about 5 to 1. Long leverage is in the 73rd percentile of the past year (94th over 5 years). Short leverage is near 5-year highs (99th percentile).

UK Autumn Budget preview: forecast changes likely cut fiscal headroom from 20bn to about 15bn pounds before new policies. Tax rises are expected at around 5bn pounds, smaller than in 2024 and 2025, which sets up a difficult Spending Review next year.

SAP (Buy, PT EUR230, 10% upside): 3Q beat across all KPIs. Current cloud backlog grew 26% in constant currency versus 24.6% consensus. GS expects consensus to stay broadly unchanged and a positive share price reaction.
BESI is mixed: solid quarter with a big order beat (15% ahead of the Street), light Q4 guide on pushouts, and ASML risk pushed back. GS expects the stock to be up today given short positioning.
Maersk downgraded to Sell (PT DKK18, 25% downside) because the temporary factors tightening container markets (subdued 2026 supply growth, disruption, US restocking) are expected to fade.
Galderma beat topline by 5%, with Nemluvio 7% ahead ($302m vs $283m). Guidance was raised to 22.5%-23.5%, above GS expectations of 21-22%, driving about 2% upgrades to FY26 Street numbers.
Schindler Q3 beat by 5%, with orders 6% above consensus and over 10% organic order growth, a material acceleration from 2Q. Defensive and quality names are coming back into favor.
SEB missed by 5% on weaker core and trading income, with good cost discipline. NII missed consensus by 1%, with loan growth +4% q/q.

market_movers.rationale: Current cloud backlog beat at 26% CC growth versus 24.6% consensus. Organic CCB growth of about 25.2% showed no deceleration for a third quarter, supporting the S/4HANA migration cycle.
Container market tightness is driven by temporary factors that GS expects to fade. Implies 25% downside.
Stock rose about 5% on a solid Q3 revenue beat and Q4 guide of $73-76bn versus $73.57bn consensus.
Stock fell 7.5% despite a quarterly beat, with F2Q gross margin guide of 52.4% versus about 52% consensus.

earnings_insights: META Q3: solid revenue beat, Q4 revenue guide $73-76bn versus $73.57bn consensus. A new class of stock is coming in January 2027. Stock +5%.
TSLA: Q3 deliveries were a clear beat but were already known from early October. Qualitative commentary was more positive than in recent quarters. Stock +4%.
LRCX: beat on the quarter, F2Q gross margin guide 52.4% versus about 52% consensus, guide slightly above Street. Stock -7.5%.

SAP 3Q: current cloud backlog +26% CC versus 24.6% consensus, cloud revenue +25% to about EUR6.7bn (about 2 points ahead, with about 1 point from one-offs), total revenue EUR10.27bn, operating profit EUR3.03bn, both ahead of expectations.
BESI: small beats at gross and operating profit, orders 15% ahead of the Street, Q4 guide light due to pushouts.
Galderma: topline 5% beat, Nemluvio $302m versus $283m expected, guidance raised to 22.5%-23.5% versus GS 21-22%, about 2% upgrades to Street FY26.
Schindler Q3: 5% beat, orders 6% above consensus, over 10% organic order growth.
SEB: 5% miss on core and trading income, NII 1% below consensus, loan growth +4% q/q, with Swedish BRB +3%, CIB +6%, Baltics +10% q/q.
SPCX: strong Q3 earnings, stock +7.8%. SMCI: positive pre-announcement, stock +10%.

macro_indicators.reading: around 15bn pounds before new policies, from 24bn pounds
macro_indicators.interpretation: Weaker growth and higher rates outweigh a stronger wage projection, making tax rises likely but modest at about 5bn pounds.
Smaller than in 2024 and 2025, a low-key Budget that sets up a difficult Spending Review next year.

risk_factors: Mag7 competition concerns following SPCX results and possible source-of-funds selling ahead of expected future issuance.
Semis bounce felt underwhelming after 10 of 11 sessions lower.
Maersk: temporary supply and demand supports in container shipping are expected to fade.
UK Spending Review next year is expected to be difficult.
vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds net sold global equities heavily in October, with short sales outpacing long buys about 5 to 1.
Long leverage is in the 73rd percentile versus the past year and the 94th percentile over 5 years.
Short leverage has risen sharply and is near 5-year highs (99th percentile).
BESI is described as a consensus short, so GS expects a rise on the print given positioning.
